newsitem.title: USA: U.S. FERC rejects Primergy merger, urges new plan.
newsitem.headline: U.S. FERC rejects Primergy merger, urges new plan.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission Wednesday rejected the merger of Northern States Power Co and Wisconsin Energy Corp as it was filed and gave the parties three months to work out an acceptable plan.

The $6 billion merger of the upper Midwest utilities into a holding company called Primergy Corp would create the nation's tenth largest utility. Even if a new plan were approved, it would still needs approval from regulators in two states and several federal agencies.
The commission ordered a three-month settlement conference to develop a new plan and suggested that divestiture of some generation capacity could ease problems of market power concentration.

The commission rejected last summer's finding by a FERC administrative law judge that said the utilities' plan for an independent systems operator adequately resolved concerns of market power concentration in the Wisconsin-Upper Michigan region.
"We are resolute that we cannot determine that mergers that increase market power to unacceptable levels are in the public interest," FERC Chairman Elizabeth Moler said.
"In the three months coming, the parties are being sent away to get this right," FERC Commissioner James Hoecker said.
